work.title: Making retrieval explainable before making it clever
work.summary: Designing deterministic retrieval layers for organisations whose most important knowledge is fragmented across documents, systems, and teams.
work.context: Enterprise information work breaks down when sources are inconsistent, provenance is unclear, and an answer cannot be inspected. The engineering task is to create a dependable path from source material to a useful, attributable response.
focus: evaluation gates, provenance, and failure analysis

work.title: Treating inference performance as an architecture problem
work.summary: Engineering the path between a model and a dependable user experience: latency, throughput, cost, hardware, and operational constraints together.
work.context: Performance is rarely solved by a single model swap. It comes from making the full system observable, choosing the right execution boundary, and designing for the constraints that production actually imposes.

work.title: Turning ambiguous data problems into buildable systems
work.summary: Architecting data and AI work across high-consequence domains, where reliability, auditability, and team alignment matter as much as capability.
work.context: The hard part is often not selecting a tool. It is translating an unclear business problem into system boundaries, operating assumptions, and an execution plan that a team can own after delivery.
focus: technical strategy across engineering and stakeholders
